chunks: Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al-Jammal, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Azan is recited twice by twice, and the Iqamah is recited twice by twice'.

key_terms.مَثْنَى مَثْنَى: Twice by twice (repeated two times each)

ai.seo_question: How many times should each phrase of the Adhan and Iqamah be repeated according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the ritual precision of the Adhan and Iqamah, with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirming that each phrase is recited twice (muthanna). This ruling distinguishes the Shia practice from some Sunni schools that recite certain phrases only once, underscoring the importance of following the Imams' specific liturgical instructions. It serves as a foundational text for the fiqh of prayer calls, emphasizing the prophetic tradition preserved through the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Safwan Al Jammal who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The Azān is twice by twice, and the Iqamah is twice by twice’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from ibn abu Najran from Safwan al-Jammal who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
Adhan is twice and twice and ‘Iqamah is twice and twice.’”
